title: Pallet weight and trailer capacity
before:
1. Apply a single maximum pallet weight to every outbound load plan. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg. Use this figure as the planning weight for stability checks, weight totals and transport bookings, even when the actual pallet weighs less.

Assess each order against that limit before wrapping and staging. Reject overweight pallets for rework into compliant units. Record the verified weight in the release documentation covered under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.

2. Plan curtain-side trailer loads against payload first. Our contracted curtain-side trailers carry a payload of 24000 kg. Divide that payload by the maximum pallet weight to establish the weight-constrained limit.

Calculate 24000 kg divided by 800 kg per pallet to give 30 pallets. Treat this quotient as a hard ceiling for full-weight pallets. Do not round upward or add an additional pallet on the assumption of lighter average weight without a documented re-weigh.

3. Compare the weight result with the physical floor capacity. A trailer has 33 floor pallet positions. Position count sets the volume footprint available for standard pallets placed on the trailer bed.

Count positions from the headboard to the rear doors without double-stacking unless the load plan expressly permits it. Leave damaged floor sections empty and reduce the usable count accordingly.

4. Govern every full-weight movement by the lower of the two limits. A trailer takes at most 30 full-weight pallets (payload divided by maximum pallet weight, capped by floor positions).

Explain the outcome to loading teams in plain terms. Weight restricts the load before space does. Three floor positions remain theoretically vacant when carrying 30 pallets at 800 kg each, because adding a 31st full-weight pallet would exceed the 24000 kg payload.

5. Build mixed-weight loads within the same ceiling. Sum the actual verified weights of all pallets on the consignment. Keep the total at or below 24000 kg and the pallet count at or below 33 floor pallet positions.

Allocate heavier pallets over the axles and distribute weight evenly along the bed. Secure each row to prevent shifting during transit. Reconcile the final loaded quantity and weight against the release paperwork before closing the doors.

6. Document exceptions and partial loads consistently. Where pallets weigh less than 800 kg, more than 30 physical pallets may travel provided neither the 24000 kg payload nor the 33 floor pallet positions are exceeded.

Enter the per-pallet weights, total weight and position count on the load sheet. Retain the calculation for audit and driver handover. Escalate any request to exceed either limit through the normal dispatch control before loading.

7. Enforce the limit at staging and loading. Check pallet weights at wrapping, verify totals at staging, and re-confirm before truck departure. Refuse to load a 31st full-weight pallet onto a trailer already carrying 30 pallets at maximum weight, even where empty floor space remains visible.

title: Van and shift dispatch limit
before:
1. Use the delivery van only for small consignments that cannot justify a trailer movement. Our delivery van carries a payload of 1200 kg.
2. Plan van loading against floor space as well as weight. The delivery van has 6 pallet positions.
3. Apply the full-weight limit as the binding constraint for heavy pallets. The van takes at most 1 full-weight pallets; heavier orders go by trailer.
4. Assign any order exceeding the van limit to trailer transport under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Do not split a heavy pallet across van positions to circumvent the weight limit.
5. Stage van consignments in Zone D separately from trailer staging. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
6. Release van departures through the same dispatch control as trailers. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers.
7. Treat the van as overflow and urban-drop capacity, not as part of the per-shift pallet promise. Record van pallets separately from trailer load counts in the release documentation.
8. Plan trailer throughput from fixed door capacity. There are 4 outbound dock doors.
9. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. No inbound receiving may occupy these doors during scheduled outbound loading.
10. Schedule loading to the standard turnaround. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift.
11. Calculate the shift promise from doors multiplied by loads per shift. Outbound capacity is at most 360 full-weight pallets per shift (doors x loads per shift x pallets per trailer).
12. Commit to customers only within that ceiling. Accept additional bookings for the same shift only when a booked load cancels and the dispatcher releases the door slot.
13. Sequence staging, wrapping checks and reconciliation so each door completes its 3 loads without queuing into the next shift. Hold late-arriving trailers for the following shift rather than overloading doors, labour or yard space.
14. Coordinate van movements so they do not block trailer access to docks 5-8. Load the van from the marked staging area and dispatch it between trailer manoeuvres.
15. Report any door taken out of service, trailer rejection or labour shortfall to the dispatcher immediately. Reduce the promised pallet quantity for that shift pro rata and rebook the balance.

title: Dispatchers
before:
1. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads across all staffed shifts.
2. As scheduling owner, the dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers and maintains the daily transport plan without gaps or double bookings.
3. Within Zone D, the dispatch zone, outbound staging in front of docks 5-8 remains under dispatcher control from pallet staging through loading to departure.
4. Coordination with Zone A covers the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection, ensuring inbound arrivals do not conflict with outbound movements.
5. Across the building the dispatcher manages all 8 dock doors as a single resource, with dock doors 1-4 serving inbound receiving and dock doors 5-8 serving outbound dispatch.
6. Under PR-01 Inbound receiving, dispatchers sequence arrivals so the document check happens BEFORE unloading, and no vehicle is called to doors 1-4 without complete booking documentation.
7. Under PR-06 Outbound dispatch, dispatchers authorise each load release only when wrapping, labelling, quantity reconciliation and transport documents are complete.
8. Capacity planning uses fixed outbound throughput: there are 4 outbound dock doors and each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift.
9. Contracted curtain-side trailers used for planning carry a payload of 24000 kg and provide 33 floor pallet positions for load building.
10. For full-weight planning, a trailer takes at most 30 full-weight pallets, calculated as payload divided by maximum pallet weight and capped by floor positions.
11. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg, and the dispatcher rejects any load plan exceeding trailer payload or floor positions.
12. Local deliveries allocated to the van respect its limits: our delivery van carries a payload of 1200 kg with 6 pallet positions, and takes at most 1 full-weight pallets; heavier orders go by trailer.
13. Total outbound capacity is at most 360 full-weight pallets per shift, derived from doors x loads per shift x pallets per trailer, and dispatchers cap bookings at that ceiling.
14. Throughout the shift dispatchers work beside the shift supervisor, who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, escalating labour shortfalls, door faults and trailer rejections without delay.
15. Final accountability for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs rests with the warehouse manager, and dispatchers obtain required approvals for overtime, over-capacity bookings or exceptional movements.
16. At shift change dispatchers contribute load status, door allocation and carrier ETAs to PR-15 End-of-shift handover and remain available until the incoming team accepts control.

title: Dispatch Capacity and Release
before:
1. Harborwick provides outbound staging in Zone D in front of docks 5-8 for all scheduled dispatches. Operationally staging capacity is managed to keep staged pallets clear of dock approaches and available for prompt loading. Reliably staged loads are released in door call order to avoid congestion.

2. Altogether the building operates 8 dock doors with maintained access for concurrent inbound and outbound work. Specifically dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch and are reserved for loading and departure activities. Four outbound dock doors remain dedicated to outbound schedules during staffed shifts.

3. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads under client bookings. Carriers receive assigned doors and time slots from the dispatcher before arrival. Timely communication of slot changes keeps waiting time to a minimum.

4. Monday to Friday Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00 for dispatch operations, wrapping and loading. Following that Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, continuing outbound release without interruption. Throughout both shifts dispatcher cover remains available for door allocation and load release.

5. Per shift each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads as committed throughput. Consistently loading performance is sequenced to meet carrier windows within each shift. Beyond scheduled loads, additional movements depend on available door capacity.

6. Contracted curtain-side trailers carry a payload of 24000 kg for outbound consignments. Aboard each trailer there are 33 floor pallet positions for floor-loaded pallets. Safely loaded quantity respects both payload and floor-position limits on every departure.

7. Given a maximum pallet gross weight of 800 kg including its load, a trailer takes at most 30 full-weight pallets. Therefore outbound capacity reaches at most 360 full-weight pallets per shift across doors, loads and trailer limits. Fully laden shipments approaching these limits are planned across multiple trailers.

8. Complementing trailers, our delivery van carries a payload of 1200 kg for smaller consignments. Inside the van there are 6 pallet positions for light orders. Consequently the van takes at most 1 full-weight pallets; heavier orders go by trailer.

9. Before release toward dispatch, PR-05 Packing and labelling applies to every order container. Picked items are scan-verified BEFORE packing to confirm accuracy before cartons are closed. Afterwards PR-06 Outbound dispatch governs wrapping and load release and loading for all staged orders.

10. Using 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers, dispatch wraps every outbound pallet to stable transport condition. Moreover each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller supporting safe bridging between dock and trailer. Ultimately no load is released unless wrapping, documentation and dispatcher release are complete.

title: Operating Hours and Cut-offs
before:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. operates the warehouse on two staffed shifts, Monday to Friday.
2. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and provides full receiving, storage, picking and dispatch coverage.
3. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, and provides continued receiving, picking, packing and dispatch coverage.
4. Outside these staffed hours no inbound or outbound handling is committed unless additional working has been expressly agreed.
5. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime, and any agreed extension will be confirmed with its supervised hours.
6. The building has 8 dock doors available for scheduled carrier movements within the operating shifts.
7. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving under PR-01 Inbound receiving.
8. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.
9. There are 4 outbound dock doors, and outbound capacity is planned exclusively against those doors.
10. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers for both inbound and outbound movements.
11. Carriers must arrive within the assigned slot, as late arrival may require rescheduling to the next available door and slot.
12. For inbound receiving, the agreed intake cut-off means booked arrivals received before the cut-off enter same-shift inspection and system booking.
13. Booked arrivals received after the applicable intake cut-off will be received and processed on the next staffed shift.
14. Unbooked or early arrivals will be accommodated only where a door and handling resource remain available without displacing booked slots.
15. For outbound dispatch, the agreed order cut-off means orders released before the cut-off enter same-shift wrapping, staging and loading.
16. Orders released after the applicable dispatch cut-off roll to the next staffed dispatch wave.
17. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift, which sets the disciplined turnaround available to carriers.
18. Consequently, outbound capacity is at most 360 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated from doors, loads per shift and pallets per trailer.
19. Harborwick commits to make that per-shift capacity available when orders and transport have met the agreed cut-offs.
20. Where client volumes exceed the per-shift limit, the excess will be scheduled across following shifts or agreed overtime.
21. Agreed cut-off times apply per shift and per flow, so inbound and outbound cut-offs operate independently.
22. Changes to recurring cut-off times will be agreed in writing and applied from the next operational week unless otherwise confirmed.
23. Daily variations caused by door maintenance, labour constraints or carrier delays will be communicated promptly with a revised door and slot plan.
24. Performance against operating hours, slot adherence and cut-off application will be reported per shift in line with Chapter 1 service levels.
